Real-World Challenges and How to Avoid Them

Nepal’s FDI framework has improved dramatically. But challenges remain, and experienced investors know that preparation is what separates a smooth 2-month registration from a frustrating 6-month one.

1. Document Authentication Delays Are the Most Common Cause of Delay

Foreign company documents must be apostilled or embassy-authenticated before Nepal submission. In countries without a Nepal Embassy or Consulate nearby, finding the right authentication pathway can take 2-3 weeks. Start the authentication process before you finalise your documents. This single step, done early, saves the most time overall.

2. Investment Amount vs Injection Schedule Mismatch

Investors who apply for FDI approval for an ambitious total investment amount but then cannot meet the Stage 1 minimum injection of 25% within one year face regulatory complications. Apply for the investment amount you can realistically inject on schedule. The DoI can approve amendments to investment amounts, but this adds time and uncertainty.

3. MOA Business Description Not Matching FDI Approval

The company’s MOA must describe business activities that precisely match the FDI approval and the IEA industry classification. Draft the MOA AFTER receiving the FDI Approval Certificate, not before. A mismatch, however small, creates complications at industry registration and during DoI monitoring visits.

4. Missing the NRB 6-Month Recording Deadline

The most consequential compliance failure for foreign investors in Nepal is missing the 6-month NRB recording deadline after capital injection. This affects profit repatriation rights. Multiple investors have discovered this problem when they first tried to repatriate dividends, years after the injection. Set calendar reminders from the date of every SWIFT receipt confirmation from your Nepali bank.

5. Confusing Company Registration with Industry Registration

These are two separate steps with two separate legal effects. OCR registration makes the company a legal entity. DoI industry registration makes it an industry eligible for incentives and subject to the commencement obligation. Foreign investors who skip the DoI industry registration step discover the omission when they first try to claim tax incentives or when the DoI conducts a monitoring visit.

6. Underestimating Post-Registration Monitoring

The DoI conducts periodic monitoring visits to foreign-invested industries to verify that operations have commenced, capital has been properly injected according to the schedule, and regulatory obligations are being met. These are thorough, not courtesy calls. Maintain clean, organized records from day one and designate a responsible person (internal or external advisor) to track all compliance deadlines.

Frequently Asked Questions

1. Can a foreigner own 100% of an industry in Nepal?

Yes, in most sectors. FITTA 2019 permits 100% foreign ownership in all industries that are not on the Negative List or subject to specific foreign equity caps. A Nepali joint venture partner is not legally required in most open sectors. 100% foreign-owned companies are legally and operationally common in manufacturing, IT, healthcare, hotels, education, and most services. Sectors with equity caps include banking (49-65%), telecommunications (80%), domestic airlines (49%), and consultancy services (51%).

2. What is the minimum investment required for a foreigner to establish an industry in Nepal?

The minimum foreign investment threshold under FITTA 2019 is NPR 20,000,000 (NPR 20 million, approximately USD 150,000). This threshold was reduced from NPR 50 million in 2019 reforms. The IT sector has no minimum investment threshold for Automatic Route applications, a foreign investor can establish an IT company in Nepal with any capital amount above zero, making Nepal one of the most accessible markets in South Asia for technology startups.

3. What is the Automatic Route and how fast is it?

The Automatic Route, introduced in 2023, allows foreign investments up to NPR 500 million (approximately USD 3.8 million) to be approved by the Department of Industry through an online portal. FITTA Section 15(2) mandates a 7-working-day processing deadline for complete Automatic Route applications. In FY 2024/25, 97% of Nepal’s foreign investment commitments, approximately NPR 58 billion, came through this route. It has transformed the FDI process from a multi-month ordeal into a manageable 7-day approval.

4. Do I need a Nepali joint venture partner?

No, in most sectors. A Nepali joint venture partner is not legally required for industries not on the Negative List and not subject to foreign equity caps. 100% foreign ownership is the legal baseline for most open sectors. However, many foreign investors choose Nepali partners for practical reasons: local market relationships, land acquisition facilitation (individual foreigners cannot own land directly, only Nepali-incorporated companies can), government liaison, and cultural navigation. A Nepali partner is a business strategy decision, not a legal requirement for most sectors.

5. Which sectors are completely closed to foreign investment in Nepal?

Completely prohibited sectors include: primary agriculture (with limited export-oriented agritech exceptions), cottage and traditional handicraft industries, personal services, arms and weapons manufacturing, real estate trading (not construction), retail and domestic trading, travel agencies, trekking companies, tour guides, rural tourism and homestays, and mass communication media in Nepali language. These cannot be accessed through any ownership structure, nominee arrangement, or legal workaround.

6. How long does the complete registration process take?

For a standard Automatic Route investment with completely authenticated documents, the total process from FDI approval through NRB investment recording typically takes 2 to 3 months. The home-country document authentication process (apostille or embassy authentication) is usually the longest pre-submission stage at 2 to 4 weeks. The FDI approval itself takes only 7 working days. Sector-specific licenses add 2 to 8 additional weeks for regulated industries.

7. Can I repatriate 100% of my profits from Nepal?

Yes. FITTA 2019 Section 20 explicitly guarantees the right to repatriate 100% of dividends, profits, capital gains, and technology transfer royalties, subject to payment of all applicable Nepal taxes and NRB approval. NRB must respond to a complete repatriation application within 15 days. Investors who have properly recorded each investment injection with NRB within the 6-month deadline can repatriate without complications.

8. What is the three-stage investment injection schedule?

FITTR 2021 Rule 9 requires foreign investors to inject their approved capital in stages: at least 25% of the total approved investment within 1 year of the FDI Approval Certificate date, additional tranches within 2 years, and the remaining balance within 3 years. For investments below NPR 50 million, the schedule is more flexible. IT sector investors on the Automatic Route have no prescribed minimum per stage. Apply for only the total investment amount you can realistically inject within the prescribed schedule.

9. What tax incentives are available for foreign-invested industries?

Nepal’s incentives are substantial: manufacturing industries in mountain districts receive a 100% income tax exemption for 10 years; hill district industries receive 7 years; Terai and valley industries receive 5 years. Infrastructure industries receive a 40% income tax concession. Export manufacturers receive a 20% reduction plus 5% additional on export income. Industries in Special Economic Zones receive a 10-year full exemption, 50% reduction in years 11-15, and dividend tax exemption for the first 5 years.

10. What happens if I invest in a sector on the Negative List by mistake?

Investing in a Negative List sector without authorization violates FITTA 2019 and the Companies Act. The DoI will deny the FDI approval at the application stage. If the investment is somehow structured around the restriction using nominee arrangements, it constitutes fraud under Nepal’s laws and can result in criminal prosecution of all involved parties, forced divestiture of the investment, and potential blacklisting from future investment in Nepal. Always conduct a sector eligibility check with a qualified Nepal lawyer before committing capital.

11. Can I invest through a venture capital fund in Nepal?

Yes, from 2025. A January 2025 ordinance amended FITTA to allow foreign investors to make equity investments in Nepali companies through venture capital funds or specialized investment funds registered with Nepal’s Securities Board of Nepal (SEBON). This represents the most recent liberalization of Nepal’s FDI framework and opens a new institutional investment pathway particularly relevant for technology sector and growth equity investors.

12. What is the Investment Board Nepal (IBN) and when do I need it instead of the DoI?

The Investment Board Nepal (IBN) at Singha Durbar, Kathmandu, handles foreign investments above NPR 6 billion (approximately USD 45 million) and certain nationally strategic projects such as large hydropower, major infrastructure, and special economic zone development. For the vast majority of foreign investors, those investing below NPR 6 billion, the Department of Industry (DoI) at the OSSC, Tripureshwor, is the correct and sole approval authority.

Conclusion: Nepal Is Open, Do It Right

The numbers from FY 2024/25 are clear: NPR 58 billion in commitments, 97% through the Automatic Route, China and India leading but investors from 30+ countries participating. The 2019 FITTA reforms, the 2023 Automatic Route launch, the minimum capital reduction to NPR 20 million, the elimination of the provincial recommendation requirement in 2025, and the January 2025 venture capital fund amendment, these are not cosmetic changes. Nepal is actively building an investment environment that works.

But the process still rewards preparation. The investors who move through Nepal’s FDI framework in 2 to 3 months are those who authenticate documents before submitting, whose investment amounts match their actual injection capacity, whose MOA objectives align precisely with their FDI approval, and who set calendar reminders for the NRB 6-month recording deadline from day one.

The investors who take 6 to 12 months are those who discover authentication requirements after submission, who apply for larger investment amounts than they can inject on schedule, or who miss the NRB recording deadline and spend months regularizing the situation before they can even think about repatriating their first dividend.

The government has done its part. What separates successful investors from frustrated ones is preparation.”

title: Education Consultancy Registration in Nepal: Step-by-Step Guide
content:
Education consultancies are a popular way into the Nepali services market, and the sector is regulated precisely because the consequences of getting it wrong fall on students and their families. That regulation is not a barrier so much as a signal: done properly, a consultancy carries a credibility that an unregistered operation cannot claim.

This guide explains what registration involves, which approvals apply, and how to stay compliant once you are operating.

Quick answer

This article covers the complete registration and licensing process for starting an education consultancy in Nepal, including the legal framework, all 7 steps from company registration to MoSD license, required documents, government fees (NPR), timelines, TITI counselor requirements, MOU requirements, renewal rules, penalties for non-compliance, and FAQs. Researched and verified against 2025 regulations by Pluto Associates, Kathmandu.

Introduction: Nepal’s Booming Education Consultancy Sector

Nepal is one of the highest per-capita exporters of students for overseas higher education in Asia. Every year, hundreds of thousands of Nepali students aspire to study in countries such as Australia, the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, Japan, South Korea, and Germany. This extraordinary demand has created a thriving education consultancy industry, one that has grown dramatically over the past decade and continues to expand.

An education consultancy in Nepal acts as the critical bridge between aspiring students and foreign universities and colleges. These firms provide services that range from country and course selection, application preparation, scholarship guidance, and visa filing support, to pre-departure orientation and post-arrival assistance. Given the life-altering nature of this guidance, the Government of Nepal has established a comprehensive regulatory framework to ensure that only properly qualified, licensed, and financially stable firms can operate in this sector.

The scale of enforcement has intensified dramatically in 2025. According to recent regulatory data, over 4,100 education consultancies were found operating across Nepal without proper registration or a valid license. In a single week during July 2025, the Department of Commerce, Supplies and Consumer Protection collected fines totalling NPR 605,000 from unlicensed consultancies in Kathmandu alone. Operating without a valid license now carries penalties of NPR 50,000 to NPR 100,000 per violation, plus the risk of immediate closure.

For entrepreneurs seeking to enter this lucrative sector, obtaining the proper registrations and licenses is not optional, it is the non-negotiable foundation of any sustainable education consultancy business in Nepal. This guide provides a complete, step-by-step roadmap through the entire process.

Legal Framework: Laws and Governing Authorities

The education consultancy sector in Nepal is regulated by a layered set of laws that operate at both the national and provincial level. Following Nepal’s transition to a federal system, licensing authority has been transferred from the central government to provincial governments. Understanding this structure is essential before commencing the registration process.

2.2 Licensing Authority: An Important Recent Change

A critically important regulatory change has taken effect in Nepal’s education consultancy sector. Licensing authority has been transferred from the Ministry of Education, Science and Technology (MoEST) at the central level to the Ministry of Social Development (MoSD) in each respective province.

For education consultancies operating in Bagmati Province (Kathmandu, Lalitpur, Bhaktapur): The Ministry of Social Development, Hetauda is now the sole licensing authority. All applications must be submitted through the official ECIS (Education Consultancy Information System) Bagmati portal.

Each of Nepal’s seven provinces has its own Ministry of Social Development that handles education consultancy licensing for that province. However, the process and requirements are substantially similar across all provinces.

⚠️ Critical Update: Applications submitted to the Ministry of Education or any other ministry for Bagmati Province will not be processed. The MoSD Hetauda is the only valid authority for Bagmati Province. This change came into effect in fiscal year 2082/83 (BS).

Who Can Register an Education Consultancy in Nepal?

Any Nepali citizen or eligible foreign national (subject to restrictions) may register an education consultancy in Nepal, provided they meet the eligibility and operational requirements set out by the applicable legislation and the Ministry of Social Development.

3.1 For Nepali Citizens

Any Nepali citizen holding a valid citizenship certificate is eligible to register and operate an education consultancy.

  • The company must be registered as a Private Limited (Pvt. Ltd.) company at the Office of the Company Registrar (OCR).
  • The company must have a minimum authorized capital of NPR 5 Lakhs (NPR 500,000) and paid-up capital of NPR 5 Lakhs.

3.2 For Foreign Nationals

Foreign investment is permitted in Nepal’s education consultancy sector under FITTA 2019, but with significant restrictions:

  • Foreign nationals may invest in an education consultancy but are subject to a maximum ownership cap of 51%.
  • A Nepali partner must hold a minimum of 49% ownership in the company at all times.
  • Foreign investors must obtain Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) approval from the Department of Industry (DOI) or the Investment Board of Nepal, with prior approval from the Ministry of Education.
  • FDI approval in the education consultancy sector is subject to ministerial discretion and is not automatically granted upon application.

ℹ️ Note for Foreign Investors: Given the requirement for prior Ministry of Education approval before FDI is granted, foreign entrepreneurs are strongly advised to engage a qualified legal firm in Nepal before commencing the investment process.

Complete Step-by-Step Registration Process

The education consultancy registration process in Nepal follows a mandatory sequential order. Each step must be completed before the next can begin, as each step’s output (certificate, registration number, or document) is a required input for the following step. The complete process involves seven distinct stages across multiple government departments.

STEP 1 Company Name Reservation and Registration at the OCR

The entire registration journey begins at the Office of the Company Registrar (OCR). The first sub-step is to reserve a unique company name through the OCR’s online portal at camis.ocr.gov.np. The proposed name must:

  • Be unique and not already registered by any other company in Nepal
  • Ideally contain words such as “Education Consultancy,” “International Education,” “Global Studies,” or similar terms that clearly reflect the nature of services
  • Not contain restricted words or phrases (such as “National,” “Government,” or names of foreign countries without relevant approvals)

Once the name is approved and reserved (typically within 1-2 working days), the following legal incorporation documents must be professionally drafted:

Memorandum of Association (MOA), defines the company’s purpose, objectives, and the scope of activities

  • Articles of Association (AOA), governs the internal rules, shareholder rights, and management structure of the company

These documents, along with the application form and prescribed government fee, are submitted to the OCR. Upon verification and approval, the OCR issues the Certificate of Incorporation, which formally brings the company into legal existence.

✅ Pro Tip: Engage a legal professional to draft the MOA and AOA. These documents must correctly reflect “education consultancy services” as the company’s primary business activity. An incorrectly drafted MOA can cause rejection at later stages.

ℹ️ Timeline: Name reservation: 1-2 working days. Full company registration: 3-5 working days after document submission.

STEP 2 Tax Registration: PAN and VAT at the Inland Revenue Department

Immediately following company registration at the OCR, the newly incorporated company must obtain tax registration from the Inland Revenue Department (IRD). Two types of tax registration are relevant:

Tax registration must be completed at the Inland Revenue Office covering the area where the company’s registered address is located. The process requires submitting the company registration certificate, MOA, AOA, citizenship documents of shareholders, and proof of office address.

ℹ️ Timeline: PAN and VAT registration: 5-10 working days.

STEP 3 Ward Office Registration and Business Operation License

Following tax registration, the company must register with the Ward Office of the relevant local government (municipality or rural municipality) where the company’s office is physically located. This process produces a Business Operation License (Sanchalana Anumati Patra) from the Ward Office.

Documents typically required for Ward Office registration include the company registration certificate, PAN certificate, office rent agreement, and citizenship copies of the directors. The Ward Office may conduct a physical visit to the office premises before issuing the license.

ℹ️ Timeline: 3-5 working days.

STEP 4 Corporate Bank Account and Share Registry

The company must open a corporate bank account at any commercial bank in Nepal in the company’s name. Once the bank account is active, the required investment amount must be injected into the account, a minimum of NPR 5 Lakhs (NPR 500,000) as paid-up capital.

Following confirmation that the investment has been deposited, the company must return to the OCR to obtain the Share Registry Certificate (also called the Share Darta). This certificate records the official shareholding structure of the company and is a mandatory document at the MoSD licensing stage.

✅ Important: Ensure the investment amount is remitted via proper banking channels and that the bank can issue a certificate confirming the account operation and balance. This is a specific document required at the MoSD licensing stage.

📌 Initial Compliance: Nepal’s Companies Act requires newly incorporated companies to complete initial compliance procedures (including filing of statutory documents) within 3 months of the date of company registration. Do not delay this step.

ℹ️ Timeline: Bank account opening: 3-7 working days. Share registry from OCR: 2-5 working days after investment confirmation.

STEP 5 ECIS Portal Registration and Online Application to MoSD

With company registration, tax registration, Ward Office registration, and the Share Registry all completed, the company is now eligible to apply for the education consultancy operating license from the Ministry of Social Development. For Bagmati Province, this application is submitted exclusively through the ECIS (Education Consultancy Information System) Bagmati portal.

The ECIS portal is the official online platform operated by the Ministry of Social Development, Hetauda, for managing all education consultancy licensing applications. Applicants must:

  1. Create an account on the ECIS portal and provide company details including name, location, shareholders, and authorized capital.
  2. Complete the online application form (Schedule 1 of the Ministry of Social Development) with all required contact details and company information.
  3. Upload all required supporting documents in the formats specified by the portal.
  4. Pay the prescribed government application fee of NPR 15,000 (updated for fiscal year 2082/83) and upload proof of payment.
  5. Submit the application and obtain a File Registration Number for tracking purposes.

⚠️ Non-Refundable Fee: The NPR 15,000 application fee is non-refundable. If your application is rejected, the fee is forfeited and you must pay NPR 15,000 again upon reapplication. Ensure all documents are complete and compliant before submitting.

ℹ️ Timeline: ECIS portal registration and application submission: 1-2 working days (assuming all documents are prepared in advance).

STEP 6 MoSD Physical Inspection of Office Premises

Upon receiving and reviewing the application, the Ministry of Social Development will schedule a physical inspection of the education consultancy’s registered office premises. This inspection is mandatory and cannot be waived under any circumstances. The MoSD inspection team will verify:

That the office is in a commercial location (residential premises are generally not acceptable)

  • That the office is operational and appropriately equipped for student counselling
  • That the minimum space requirements are met, with adequate seating for student consultations
  • That the TITI-certified counselors are present and can be interviewed by the inspection team
  • That the office displays required information about services, fees, and partner universities transparently
  • That all physical infrastructure standards set by the Ministry are met

The inspection team may also interview the counselors about their qualifications, experience, and knowledge of the countries and universities they represent. Counselors must hold valid TITI certification and must be able to demonstrate competence in student counselling.

⚠️ Inspection Failure: If the inspection reveals that the office does not meet the Ministry’s standards, or if the TITI-certified counselors are not present, the application will be rejected. Reapplication requires paying the NPR 15,000 fee again.

ℹ️ Timeline: Inspection scheduling: 7-14 days after application acceptance. Inspection itself: typically half a day.

STEP 7 License Issuance from the Ministry of Social Development

Upon successful completion of the physical inspection and verification of all documents, the Ministry of Social Development issues the official Education Consultancy Operating License. For Bagmati Province applicants, this is the MOSD Bagmati Consultancy License, the document that authorises the company to legally operate as an education consultancy in Nepal.

The license is issued both digitally (via the ECIS portal) and as a physical certificate dispatched to the company’s registered address. The license specifies the validity period (one fiscal year) and any conditions attached to the authorization.

✔ You’re Licensed! Upon receiving the MoSD license, your education consultancy is fully authorised to operate legally in Nepal. You may now begin serving students, entering into formal agreements with foreign universities, and marketing your services publicly.

ℹ️ Timeline: License issuance: 3-7 working days after successful inspection.

Complete Document Checklist

Submitting a complete, accurate, and consistent set of documents is the single most important factor in ensuring a smooth application process. The following is the comprehensive checklist for the MoSD license application. Documents for earlier stages (OCR registration, PAN/VAT) are not repeated here, as they will already have been obtained.

6.1 Company Documents

  1. Duly completed application form (Schedule 1 from the Ministry of Social Development website)
  2. Copy of Certificate of Company Registration from the OCR
  3. Memorandum of Association (MOA), certified copy
  4. Articles of Association (AOA), certified copy
  5. Share Registry Certificate (Darta Pramaanpatra) from the OCR
  6. PAN Certificate from the Inland Revenue Department
  7. VAT Registration Certificate from the Inland Revenue Department
  8. Ward Office Business Operation License
  9. Receipt confirming payment of the NPR 15,000 application fee
  10. Tax clearance certificate from the Inland Revenue Department (mandatory if the company has been registered for more than one year)
  11. Audit report with balance sheet (if the company is more than one year old)
  12. Company bank account operation certificate

6.2 Office Premises Documents

  1. House rent agreement for the office premises, valid for a minimum of 2 years
  2. Tax payment slip for the rented premises
  3. Citizenship certificate of the house/property owner
  4. Lalpurja (land ownership certificate) or other valid proof of property ownership

6.3 Counselor Documents (for each of the 2 required counselors)

  1. TITI certification certificate (from the Training Institute for Technical Instruction, Sanothimi, Bhaktapur), the only certification accepted by MoSD
  2. Bachelor’s degree certificate or higher academic transcripts
  3. Citizenship certificate of the counselor
  4. Offer letter from the company and acceptance letter signed by the counselor
  5. Language proficiency certificate (if the counselor is also responsible for language test preparation programs) showing a minimum 75% pass score

6.4 Foreign University MOU Documents (for each of the 2 required MOUs)

  1. Original or certified copy of the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the foreign university
  2. Profile of the foreign university (with accreditation details)
  3. Representation letter from the foreign university confirming the partnership

6.5 Additional Documents for Language or Test Preparation Programs

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher academic transcripts of the language instructor
  • Citizenship certificate of the language instructor
  • Offer and acceptance letters for the language instructor
  • Language proficiency certificate showing a minimum 75% pass score

Understanding the TITI Counselor Requirement

The requirement for TITI-certified counselors is one of the most distinctive and often overlooked aspects of the education consultancy licensing process in Nepal. The Training Institute for Technical Instruction (TITI), located in Sanothimi, Bhaktapur, is Nepal’s premier vocational and technical training institution, established in 1991 under the CTEVT Act 1988.

TITI provides specialized training programs for education counselors that cover the knowledge and skills required to competently guide students about international study options, application processes, visa requirements, and life abroad. Completion of a TITI training program and receipt of the TITI certificate is a non-negotiable requirement for at least two staff members of every licensed education consultancy in Nepal.

7.1 TITI Counselor Eligibility Requirements

  • Minimum educational qualification: Bachelor’s degree in any field
  • The counselor must be formally employed by the education consultancy (evidenced by an offer letter and acceptance letter)
  • The counselor must complete a TITI training program conducted at Sanothimi, Bhaktapur
  • TITI certification must be current and valid at the time of the MoSD application and inspection

License Renewal: Maintaining Legal Compliance

The education consultancy license issued by the Ministry of Social Development is valid for one financial year (Nepali fiscal year: mid-July to mid-July, i.e. Shrawan to Ashadh). It must be renewed annually to maintain the legal right to operate.

10.1 Renewal Deadline

License renewal must be completed within 3 months of the end of each financial year, that is, before the end of Ashoj (approximately mid-October) of each year. A grace period of 15 days is provided after the expiry of the license, during which operations are still legally permitted. However, operations beyond this grace period without a renewed license constitute a punishable offence.

10.2 Documents Required for Renewal

  • Latest tax clearance certificate from the Inland Revenue Department
  • Audit report with balance sheet for the most recently completed financial year
  • Updated MoSD application form (Schedule 1)
  • Receipt of renewal fee payment (NPR 15,000 for FY 2082/83)
  • Updated MOU documents if any foreign university partnerships have changed
  • Updated TITI counselor certificates if any counselors have changed
  • Updated house rent agreement if the current agreement has expired

⚠️ Late Renewal Consequences: Operating an education consultancy with an expired license is a violation of the Education Consultancy Service Directive 2073. Penalties range from NPR 50,000 to NPR 100,000 and may include immediate closure of the business by the Department of Commerce, Supplies and Consumer Protection. Begin renewal preparation at least 60 days before the renewal deadline.

ECAN Membership: Optional but Recommended

The Education Consultancy Association of Nepal (ECAN) is the industry’s primary professional association, representing education consultancies across Nepal. While ECAN membership is not legally mandatory for obtaining or maintaining an education consultancy license, it offers significant practical benefits:

Industry credibility: ECAN membership signals to students and foreign universities that the consultancy adheres to professional standards and ethical practices.

  • Networking: Access to a network of fellow consultancy owners, which facilitates knowledge sharing, referral partnerships, and collective advocacy.
  • Updates: ECAN keeps members informed of regulatory changes, new country study opportunities, and changes to foreign university admission requirements.
  • Dispute resolution: ECAN provides a framework for resolving disputes between members and between consultancies and students.
  • Events and training: ECAN organises education fairs, university representative visits, and counselor training programmes.

For a newly established education consultancy seeking to build trust with students and foreign institutional partners quickly, ECAN membership is a worthwhile early investment in professional credibility.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

1. Is an education consultancy license mandatory in Nepal?

Yes, absolutely. The Education Consultancy Service Directive 2073 (2016) requires every education consultancy operating in Nepal to hold a valid license from the relevant Provincial Ministry of Social Development. Operating without a license is a punishable offence.

2. Which ministry issues the education consultancy license in Kathmandu?

The Ministry of Social Development (MoSD), Hetauda, is the sole licensing authority for education consultancies in Bagmati Province, which includes Kathmandu, Lalitpur, and Bhaktapur. Applications must be submitted through the ECIS Bagmati portal.

3. Can I use my home address as the registered office?

Generally, no. The Ministry of Social Development requires education consultancies to operate from a commercial office space. Residential addresses are typically not acceptable. The office must be in a proper commercial location and the rent agreement must be for a minimum of 2 years.

4. What exactly is the TITI certification and where do I get it?

The TITI certification is a professional counselor qualification issued by the Training Institute for Technical Instruction (TITI) located in Sanothimi, Bhaktapur. It is obtained by completing a specialized training program at TITI. This is the only certification accepted by MoSD for education consultancy licensing, no other certification, however prestigious, is accepted as a substitute.

5. How many MOU agreements with foreign universities do I need?

A minimum of two (2) Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) with foreign universities are required. These must be current, signed agreements that the MoSD can verify. Expired MOUs or unsigned draft agreements are not acceptable.

6. Can I run an education consultancy as a sole trader or partnership firm?

No. The regulatory framework explicitly requires that all education consultancies in Nepal be registered as Private Limited (Pvt. Ltd.) companies with the Office of the Company Registrar. Sole traders and partnership firms cannot obtain an education consultancy license.

7. How long does the complete registration process take?

With complete preparation (TITI-certified counselors already hired, MOUs already signed, office fully set up), the process typically takes 6-8 weeks. Without this advance preparation, the process commonly takes 2-4 months, primarily due to the time required for TITI counselor training and MOU procurement.

8. What happens if my application is rejected by MoSD?

If your application is rejected, MoSD will specify the reason(s) for rejection through the ECIS portal. The NPR 15,000 application fee is non-refundable. You may reapply after addressing all rejection reasons, but must pay the NPR 15,000 fee again upon reapplication.

9. Can I register an education consultancy as a foreign national?

Foreign nationals can invest in an education consultancy in Nepal under FITTA 2019, but with a maximum ownership of 51%. A Nepali partner must hold at least 49%. FDI approval from the Department of Industry (with prior Ministry of Education consent) is required. Given these complexities, foreign investors are strongly advised to engage a qualified Nepal law firm before proceeding.

10. How often must I renew the license?

The license must be renewed annually, within 3 months of the end of the Nepali fiscal year, specifically, before the end of Ashoj (mid-October). A 15-day grace period is available after expiry, but operating beyond this grace period is a punishable offence.

Conclusion: Invest in Compliance, Build a Lasting Business

Nepal’s education consultancy sector represents one of the country’s most dynamic and commercially promising service industries. With thousands of Nepali students seeking guidance about overseas education every year, a properly licensed and professionally managed education consultancy can build a highly profitable and meaningful business.

However, the regulatory framework governing this sector is detailed, sequential, and actively enforced. The seven-stage process, from company registration at the OCR through to license issuance by the Ministry of Social Development, demands careful preparation, complete documentation, TITI-certified professional staff, and genuine international university partnerships. Shortcuts or attempts to operate without full compliance carry significant financial and legal consequences.

title: Registering a Travel, Tours & Trekking Agency in Nepal

Trekking agencies belong to a category that looks simple from the outside and is not. The sector is open and well established, and Nepal has spent decades welcoming visitors who want to walk its mountains. At the same time, tourism is one of the areas the law reserves most carefully, because the work involves safety, foreign visitors and the country’s most treasured landscapes.

Introduction: Nepal’s Tourism Sector and Why Proper Registration Matters

Nepal’s mountains are among the most sought-after destinations on earth. Mount Everest, Annapurna, Langtang, Mustang, Kanchenjunga, the names alone carry a gravitational pull that brings trekkers, climbers, cultural travellers, and adventure seekers from over 100 countries every year. Tourism contributes approximately 7.9% of Nepal’s GDP and supports over one million jobs directly and indirectly. It is, without exaggeration, one of the most important pillars of Nepal’s economy.

Behind every successful trekking expedition, every cultural tour, every helicopter ride to Everest Base Camp, and every whitewater rafting adventure, there is a registered agency. These agencies are not just commercial entities, they are the legally accountable intermediaries between Nepal’s extraordinary natural and cultural landscape and the travellers who come to experience it. They arrange permits, hire licensed guides, book lodges, coordinate logistics, and ensure that visitors are safe and supported throughout their journey.

Operating a travel, tours, or trekking agency in Nepal without proper registration is not just a legal risk, it is a practical one. Unregistered agencies cannot issue official receipts, cannot apply for restricted area trekking permits on behalf of their clients, cannot be listed on the Nepal Tourism Board or official platforms, and cannot build the institutional credibility that international tour operators and travel companies require before partnering with Nepal-based agencies.

The regulatory landscape: Tourism in Nepal is a highly regulated sector. The primary licensing authority is the Department of Tourism (DoT) under the Ministry of Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation. The registration process involves multiple government offices, specific capital requirements, physical office standards, qualified staff requirements, and a bank guarantee that demonstrates the agency’s financial credibility. Foreign Nationals and Tourism Agencies: A Critical Legal Restriction

This section addresses one of the most important, and most frequently misunderstood, aspects of Nepal’s tourism agency registration framework. If you are a foreign national considering registering a travel, tours, or trekking agency in Nepal, read this section carefully before proceeding.

⚠️ Tourism Is on the FITTA Negative List: Travel agencies, tour operators, and trekking agencies are explicitly listed on the Negative List of the Foreign Investment and Technology Transfer Act (FITTA) 2019. This means that foreign nationals and foreign companies CANNOT directly invest in, own, or register a travel, tours, or trekking agency in Nepal. This is not a restriction that can be waived, worked around, or negotiated. It is a statutory prohibition.

4.1 What Foreign Nationals Cannot Do

  • Directly register a travel, tours, or trekking agency as a sole owner
  • Hold a majority share in a travel or trekking agency
  • Form a joint venture with a Nepali partner while holding any ownership share in a tourism agency
  • Use a Nepali nominee as a front while retaining beneficial ownership, this constitutes fraud and exposes both parties to criminal liability

4.2 What Foreign Nationals Can Do

  • Appoint a distributor or agent: Foreign tour operators and travel companies can market their services in Nepal by executing a formal distributorship or agency agreement with a registered Nepali tourism agency. The Nepali agency acts as the local representative and is responsible for regulatory compliance.
  • Employ foreign staff: A Nepali-owned tourism agency can employ qualified foreign nationals in specialist roles (mountain guides, specialist instructors, etc.) subject to work permit and visa requirements.
  • Partner with registered Nepali agencies: Foreign tourism companies commonly partner with Nepali agencies through commercial agreements for ground handling, tour packages, and trekking logistics. The Nepali agency handles all government-facing activities, while the foreign partner focuses on marketing and client acquisition abroad.

✅ Foreign Entrepreneurs’ Realistic Option: If you are a foreign national who wants to build a tourism business focused on Nepal, the practical route is to build a strong commercial partnership with a properly registered Nepali agency rather than attempting direct ownership. Many of Nepal’s most successful tourism agencies operate in exactly this model.

Complete 7-Step Registration Process

The tourism agency registration process in Nepal follows a strict sequential order across multiple government offices. Each step’s output, a certificate, a letter, a receipt, becomes a mandatory input for the next step. Approaching any authority out of sequence will result in rejection and wasted time.

STEP 1 Company Name Reservation and OCR Registration

The journey begins at the Office of the Company Registrar (OCR). Your proposed agency must be incorporated as a Private Limited Company before any subsequent steps can proceed. A sole proprietorship or partnership structure is not eligible for a DoT tourism license, the Private Limited Company structure is the standard and required form.

Name Selection

Choose a company name that clearly reflects the nature of your tourism business. Including words like “Travel,” “Tours,” “Trekking,” “Expeditions,” or “Adventures” in the name not only communicates your business immediately to potential clients but also helps improve online search visibility. Check name availability at camis.ocr.gov.np before preparing documents.

OCR Registration Requirements

The MOA and AOA must clearly state tourism-related business objectives: travel agency services, tour operations, trekking, mountaineering assistance, or whatever combination of activities you intend to conduct. A vague or incorrect business objective in the MOA can cause rejection at the DoT stage.

Documents required for OCR registration:

  1. Completed CAMIS portal application form
  2. Memorandum of Association (MOA), stating tourism as the primary business objective
  3. Articles of Association (AOA)
  4. Citizenship certificates of all shareholders/promoters (plus photocopies)
  5. Passport-sized photographs of all shareholders/promoters
  6. Office lease agreement
  7. Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) for authenticated submission
  8. OCR registration fee payment receipt

✅ Capital Structure: Register with an authorized capital of at least NPR 25 lakhs (NPR 2,500,000) from the outset. This avoids the need to amend your MOA later when the DoT requires proof of NPR 25 lakh paid-up capital.

ℹ️ Timeline: OCR name reservation: 1-2 working days. Company registration: 7-10 working days from complete submission.

STEP 2 PAN, VAT Registration and Ward Office Permit

Immediately after receiving the OCR Registration Certificate, complete the following three registrations in parallel where possible:

PAN Registration (Inland Revenue Department)

Register for a Permanent Account Number (PAN) at the Inland Revenue Department (ird.gov.np). Tourism agencies are required to register for VAT in addition to PAN, this is mandatory regardless of projected annual turnover, because tourism services are VAT-applicable in Nepal. The VAT rate applicable to tourism services is 13%.

Ward Office Business Operation Permit

Register the agency with the Ward Office (Wada Karyalaya) of the municipality where the office is located. Submit the OCR Registration Certificate, PAN certificate, and office lease agreement. The Ward Office may inspect the premises before issuing the Business Operation Permit. This permit must be renewed annually.

ℹ️ Timeline: PAN and VAT: 3-5 working days. Ward Office permit: 3-7 working days.

STEP 3 Create Company Stamp and Open Corporate Bank Account

Once PAN is obtained, have a company rubber stamp designed and manufactured. The stamp must include:

  • The full registered company name
  • The company’s OCR registration number
  • The company’s PAN number
  • The registered office address

Open a corporate bank account at any commercial bank in Nepal. The account will be used for:

  • Depositing the NPR 25 lakh minimum paid-up capital (which must be reflected in the company’s bank account certificate)
  • Day-to-day agency operations

The bank will require the OCR Registration Certificate, PAN certificate, MOA and AOA, and the Board Resolution authorizing the designated signatories to operate the account.

ℹ️ Bank Guarantee: At this stage, also request your bank to prepare the NPR 5 lakh Bank Guarantee Letter in favour of the Department of Tourism, Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu, Nepal. This is a separate instrument from the corporate bank account and may take 5-10 working days to prepare.

STEP 4 Industry Registration at the Department of Industry (DoI)

Before approaching the Department of Tourism, tourism agencies must register as an industry at the Department of Industry (DoI) under the Industrial Enterprises Act 2076. This step is often overlooked by first-time applicants, causing rejection at the DoT stage.

Submit to the DoI:

  1. OCR Registration Certificate
  2. MOA and AOA
  3. PAN certificate
  4. Citizenship certificates of directors
  5. Office lease agreement
  6. Application form for industry registration

The DoI reviews the application and issues the Industry Registration Certificate, which confirms that the tourism agency is formally registered as a service industry in Nepal.

ℹ️ Timeline: Industry registration at DoI: 7-10 working days.

STEP 5 Obtain Recommendation from the Provincial Tourism Office

Before the central Department of Tourism processes your license application, you must obtain a recommendation letter from the Provincial Tourism Office of the province where your agency’s head office is located. For agencies in Kathmandu (Bagmati Province), this means the Bagmati Province Tourism Office.

The Provincial Tourism Office reviews the application documents and, if satisfied with the agency’s compliance with basic requirements (company registration, capital, office standards), issues a recommendation letter supporting the license application.

Submit to the Provincial Tourism Office:

  1. Application letter requesting recommendation
  2. OCR Registration Certificate
  3. Industry Registration Certificate from DoI
  4. PAN and VAT certificates
  5. Ward Office Business Operation Permit
  6. Office lease agreement (minimum 5 years)
  7. Citizenship certificates of directors
  8. Bank certificate confirming paid-up capital of NPR 25 lakhs
  9. Staff list with qualifications and certificates

✅ Inspection at this Stage: The Provincial Tourism Office may conduct a physical inspection of your office premises before issuing the recommendation letter. Ensure the office is fully set up, furniture, signage, computer equipment, telephone, and proper branding, before requesting this inspection.

ℹ️ Timeline: Provincial Tourism Office recommendation: 7-14 working days.

STEP 6 Submit Tourism License Application to the Department of Tourism

With all documents and the Provincial Tourism Office recommendation in hand, submit the formal tourism agency license application to the Department of Tourism at Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu. This is the culminating step that produces the official tourism agency license.

Complete document checklist for the DoT application:

  1. Prescribed DoT application form (obtained from the DoT office at Bhrikutimandap)
  2. Application letter on company letterhead, addressed to the Director General, Department of Tourism
  3. OCR Company Registration Certificate (certified copy)
  4. MOA and AOA (certified copies)
  5. Industry Registration Certificate from the Department of Industry
  6. PAN certificate (certified copy)
  7. VAT registration certificate (certified copy)
  8. Ward Office Business Operation Permit
  9. Provincial Tourism Office recommendation letter (original)
  10. Office lease agreement (minimum 5 years, original or certified copy)
  11. Bank Guarantee Letter of NPR 5,00,000 in favour of the Department of Tourism (original from bank)
  12. Bank certificate confirming minimum paid-up capital of NPR 25,00,000 is deposited in the company’s corporate account
  13. Citizenship certificates of all directors (certified copies)
  14. Passport-sized photographs of all directors (2 each)
  15. Photographs of the office premises, exterior signboard, interior layout, reception area
  16. List of staff members with their qualifications and relevant certificates
  17. Commitment letter / Declaration signed by the company’s directors confirming compliance with all DoT regulations
  18. Tourism license fee payment receipt (NPR 25,000, paid at the DoT revenue counter)

For trekking agencies or combined agencies, additionally submit:

  • Certificates of qualified trekking guides on staff (NATHM or equivalent certification)
  • TAAN membership certificate (if already obtained)
  • Evidence of safety equipment for trekking operations

DoT Inspection

Following application submission, the Department of Tourism schedules a physical inspection of the agency’s office premises. DoT inspectors verify:

  • That the office is commercial (not residential) and meets the minimum 200 sq. ft. space requirement
  • That the office has proper signage displaying the company name and registration number
  • That the office has adequate furniture, communication equipment, and operational infrastructure
  • That qualified staff are present at the office during inspection hours
  • That the company’s tourism-related promotional materials are available

⚠️ Inspection Failure: A failed DoT inspection means the license application is paused until deficiencies are corrected. The NPR 25,000 license fee is generally not refunded. Address all potential deficiencies before the inspection is scheduled.

ℹ️ Timeline: DoT review and inspection: 15-20 working days from complete application submission.

STEP 7 Receive the Tourism License and Begin Operations

Upon successful completion of the DoT inspection and verification of all documents, the Department of Tourism issues the Tourism Agency License. This license is the definitive government authorization to operate a travel, tours, or trekking agency in Nepal.

The license specifies:

  • The registered company name and registration number
  • The category of tourism agency (Travel Agency, Tour Operator, Trekking Agency, or Combined)
  • The license issue date and expiry date (5 years from issue)
  • The license number (which must appear on all agency correspondence and marketing materials)

✔ Licensed and Ready! With the DoT Tourism License in hand, your agency is fully authorized to operate legally. You can now accept clients, arrange trekking permits, book hotels and transportation, market your services nationally and internationally, and be listed on the Nepal Tourism Board’s official directories.

ℹ️ Total Timeline: End-to-end from OCR application to DoT license: 45-60 working days for a well-prepared application. Allow 60-80 working days if any government office requests additional information.

Tourism License Validity and Renewal

8.1 License Duration

Under Rule 7 of the Travel and Trekking Agency Rules 2062, the tourism agency license is valid for 5 (five) years from the date of issuance. This is a significantly longer initial validity than many other business licenses in Nepal, a recognition that tourism is a long-term investment sector.

8.2 Renewal Procedure

The license must be renewed before its expiry date. The renewal application must be submitted to the Department of Tourism along with:

  • Renewal application form (prescribed format from DoT)
  • Original tourism license
  • Updated company registration certificate
  • Updated PAN and VAT certificates
  • Latest tax clearance certificate from IRD
  • Updated bank guarantee letter (NPR 5 lakhs, renewed for a further period)
  • Updated Ward Office Business Operation Permit
  • Renewal fee payment receipt (NPR 25,000)
  • Annual compliance report / business activity summary

Special Requirements for Trekking Agencies

Trekking agencies have additional requirements beyond the standard tourism agency registration. If your agency will organize trekking expeditions, the core activity of the Himalayan tourism sector, these specific requirements apply.

9.1 TAAN Membership

The Trekking Agencies’ Association of Nepal (TAAN) is the primary industry association for trekking agencies. While TAAN membership is not strictly legally mandatory for obtaining a Department of Tourism trekking license, it is effectively essential in practice for two reasons:

  • Client trust: International tour operators and travel companies who refer trekking clients to Nepal-based agencies routinely require TAAN membership as a baseline credibility indicator.
  • Insurance and industry support: TAAN membership provides access to group insurance arrangements, industry advocacy, training programmes, and the collective purchasing power of Nepal’s trekking industry.

TAAN membership applications are submitted to the TAAN Secretariat at Maligaon, Kathmandu. Membership requires payment of annual membership fees and evidence of DoT registration.

9.2 Licensed Trekking Guides

Trekking agencies must employ or engage licensed, certified trekking guides for all trekking operations. Trekking guide certification is issued by:

  • Nepal Academy of Tourism and Hotel Management (NATHM): The primary certification body for tourism professionals in Nepal. NATHM offers trekking guide training programmes and issues certificates recognized by the DoT.
  • Trekking Agencies’ Association of Nepal (TAAN): TAAN also runs guide training and certification programmes recognized by the industry.

At least one certified trekking guide must be on staff (not just on casual contract) at the time of the DoT inspection. The guide’s certificate must be submitted with the registration documents.

9.3 Trekking Permits for Restricted Areas

Nepal’s trekking network is divided into free trekking areas (where standard TIMS cards suffice) and restricted area trekking routes (which require special permits). Restricted areas include:

  • Upper Mustang
  • Upper Dolpo
  • Manaslu Conservation Area
  • Tsum Valley
  • Kanchenjunga Conservation Area (certain zones)
  • Humla (Limi Valley and Simikot)
  • Nar-Phu Valley
  • Dolpa (Upper and Lower)

Clients trekking in restricted areas must obtain special trekking permits through a registered trekking agency from the Department of Immigration. Unregistered agencies cannot apply for restricted area permits on behalf of their clients. This is one of the most commercially significant advantages of proper registration.

9.4 The Trekkers’ Information Management System (TIMS)

All foreign trekkers in Nepal (and Nepali trekkers in certain conservation areas) must carry a TIMS (Trekkers’ Information Management System) card. Registered trekking agencies can issue TIMS cards to their clients through the TAAN/NTB system. Unregistered agencies cannot issue TIMS cards, which is a critical service failure that professional clients will immediately recognize.

9.5 Safety and Insurance Obligations

The DoT and TAAN require that trekking agencies maintain minimum safety standards for their operations:

  • Professional liability insurance coverage (minimum NPR 2,000,000 for trekking agencies)
  • Insurance coverage for trekking guides and porters engaged on each expedition
  • First aid equipment and basic emergency medical protocols
  • Communication systems (radio/satellite phone) for remote area treks
  • Compliance with DoT-issued safety guidelines for high-altitude and adventure trekking

Himalayan Rescue Association (HRA)

Relevant for agencies operating in high-altitude trekking areas. HRA provides medical support and altitude sickness information.

himalayanrescue.org

Frequently Asked Questions

1. Can a foreign national register a travel or trekking agency in Nepal?

No. Travel agencies, tour operators, and trekking agencies are explicitly listed on the Negative List of Nepal’s Foreign Investment and Technology Transfer Act (FITTA) 2019. Foreign nationals cannot directly own, invest in, or register a tourism agency in Nepal. Foreign tourism companies wishing to operate in Nepal must work through a registered Nepali agency under a commercial distributorship or agency agreement.

2. How much capital is needed to register a trekking or travel agency in Nepal?

The minimum paid-up capital required is NPR 25,00,000 (NPR 25 lakhs). This amount must be deposited in the company’s corporate bank account and a bank certificate confirming the deposit must be submitted to the Department of Tourism as part of the license application. Additionally, a bank guarantee of NPR 5,00,000 (NPR 5 lakhs) in favour of the Department of Tourism must be obtained from a licensed commercial bank.

3. How long does the complete registration process take?

The complete process, from OCR company registration through to DoT tourism license issuance, typically takes 45 to 60 working days for a well-prepared application with all documents complete. If any government office requests additional information or documents, or if the DoT inspection reveals deficiencies requiring correction, the timeline can extend to 60 to 80 working days.

4. How long is the tourism agency license valid?

The tourism agency license issued by the Department of Tourism is valid for 5 (five) years from the date of issuance. It must be renewed before expiry by paying a renewal fee of NPR 25,000. Late renewal attracts surcharges (25% if within 3 months of expiry, 50% if between 3 and 6 months after expiry), and the license is automatically cancelled if not renewed within 6 months of expiry.

5. Do I need a physical office to register a travel agency in Nepal?

Yes. The Department of Tourism requires all registered tourism agencies to maintain a physical commercial office space that meets minimum standards. The office must be a commercial premises (not residential), at least 200 square feet in size, with proper signage displaying the company name, adequate furniture and communication facilities, and a separate toilet/washroom. Home-based offices are not permitted. The lease agreement must cover a minimum of 5 years.

6. Is TAAN membership mandatory for trekking agencies?

TAAN (Trekking Agencies’ Association of Nepal) membership is not legally mandatory under the Travel and Trekking Agency Rules 2062 for obtaining a DoT license. However, in practice, it is effectively essential for any serious trekking operation. Most international tour operators who refer clients to Nepal-based trekking agencies require TAAN membership as a baseline credibility requirement. TAAN membership also enables the agency to issue TIMS cards and access group insurance and training programmes.

7. Can one company run both travel and trekking services?

Yes. A single company can register as a Combined Travel and Trekking Agency, covering both general travel services (ticketing, hotel reservations, visa assistance) and trekking operations under one DoT license. This is the most common structure among Nepal’s full-service tourism agencies, as it allows the agency to offer clients a comprehensive range of services without needing separate registrations for each activity type.

8. What are the staff qualification requirements for a tourism agency?

At least one key staff member must hold a tourism-related degree, diploma, or recognized certification from an institution like NATHM (Nepal Academy of Tourism and Hotel Management). For trekking agencies, at least one licensed and certified trekking guide must be on staff at the time of the DoT inspection, and their certification must be submitted with the registration documents. For mountain guide agencies, NMA-certified mountain guides are required.

9. What is a TIMS card and why does it matter?

A TIMS (Trekkers’ Information Management System) card is a mandatory identification document for foreign trekkers in Nepal (and Nepali trekkers in certain conservation areas). Registered trekking agencies can issue TIMS cards to their clients through the TAAN/NTB system. Unregistered agencies cannot issue TIMS cards, which is a critical service failure that professional international clients will immediately recognize. TIMS cards provide trekker safety tracking and contribute to the management of Nepal’s trekking infrastructure.

10. What happens if I operate a tourism agency without a DoT license?

Operating a travel, tours, or trekking agency without a valid Department of Tourism license is illegal and attracts fines ranging from NPR 50,000 to NPR 5,00,000, as well as forced closure of operations. Unregistered agencies also cannot issue official receipts to clients, cannot apply for restricted area trekking permits, cannot issue TIMS cards, and cannot be listed on Nepal Tourism Board directories, making it effectively impossible to build a credible, sustainable tourism business.

11. How are VAT and taxes handled for a tourism agency?

VAT registration is mandatory for all tourism agencies in Nepal, regardless of projected annual turnover. The applicable VAT rate on tourism services is 13%. Monthly VAT returns must be filed by the 25th of the following month. The agency must also file an annual corporate income tax return (at the standard 25% rate) within 3 months of the fiscal year end. TDS must be deducted and remitted monthly on staff salaries and applicable vendor payments. Engaging a qualified chartered accountant for tax management from the beginning is strongly recommended.

12. Can I register a rafting or adventure sports agency under the same framework?

Rafting and kayak agencies follow a similar registration process to travel and trekking agencies, OCR registration, DoI industry registration, and DoT licensing. However, additional specific requirements apply: rafting permits from the Department of Tourism for each river and season of operation, certified river guides, mandatory safety equipment standards, and compliance with DoT’s adventure tourism safety guidelines. Mountain guide agencies for high-altitude climbing expeditions additionally require NMA guide certifications and expedition permits from the Ministry of Tourism.

Conclusion: Build on a Solid Foundation

Nepal’s tourism industry is one of the country’s greatest economic assets and one of its most dynamic entrepreneurial opportunities. The demand is real, the growth trajectory is clear, and the business rewards for a well-run, properly registered tourism agency are substantial.

The registration process, seven steps across multiple government offices, a significant capital commitment, physical office standards, qualified staff, and a bank guarantee, is deliberately structured to ensure that agencies entering this sector have the financial stability and professional credibility to actually serve their clients well. The barriers are real, but they are proportionate to the responsibility that tourism agencies carry: the safety, satisfaction, and experience of every client they take into Nepal’s mountains, valleys, and cultural sites.

The most common mistakes that delay or derail registration are the most avoidable: insufficient capital preparation, office premises that don’t meet DoT standards, missing or expired documents, and failure to complete the industry registration step at the Department of Industry before approaching the DoT. Address these in advance, and the process is straightforward.

title: Procedure for Obtaining a Business Visa in Nepal: Step-by-Step Guide
content:
Most foreign investors who spend real time in Nepal end up needing a business visa, and the process is more manageable than people expect once they understand which category applies to them. What tends to cause difficulty is not the visa itself, but the paperwork behind it, and the fact that the requirements differ depending on whether you are investing, working, or visiting.

This guide walks through the categories, the documents, the fees and the renewal rules, so you know what to prepare before you apply.

Quick answer

This article explains the full procedure for obtaining a Business Visa in Nepal, including who is eligible, which laws apply, what documents are required, the exact step-by-step process, government fees (in USD), processing timelines, renewal rules, and frequently asked questions. Written and verified by the legal team at Pluto Associates, Kathmandu.

Introduction: What Is a Business Visa in Nepal?

Nepal has emerged as one of South Asia’s most strategically important destinations for foreign investment and business development. Positioned between the world’s two largest economies, India and China, and endowed with vast natural resources, a growing consumer market, and a favourable foreign investment framework, Nepal offers significant opportunities for international entrepreneurs, investors, and business professionals.

A Business Visa in Nepal is a non-tourist visa category specifically issued to foreign nationals who intend to invest in, establish, operate, or represent a business or industrial enterprise in Nepal. It is distinct from a tourist visa, a work visa, or a transit visa, and obtaining one requires navigating a structured legal process involving multiple government departments.

Who issues the Business Visa? The Department of Immigration (DOI), under the Government of Nepal, is the sole authority responsible for issuing, renewing, and regulating Business Visas. However, before approaching the Department of Immigration, applicants must obtain a formal recommendation from the Department of Industry or another relevant government ministry, making the Business Visa a two-stage process.

"Nepal’s business visa framework, governed by the Immigration Act of 1992 and the Foreign Investment and Technology Transfer Act of 2019, is designed to welcome genuine foreign investors while maintaining regulatory compliance. Understanding this framework is the first step toward a successful application."

This guide, prepared by the legal professionals at Pluto Associates, provides a comprehensive, plain-language explanation of the entire procedure, from initial eligibility assessment through to visa renewal, to help foreign investors and business professionals navigate this process with clarity and confidence.

Legal Framework Governing Business Visas in Nepal

Before diving into the procedure, it is important to understand the legislative foundation that governs business visas in Nepal. Three primary laws form the legal basis:

Legislation

Year

Key Provisions Relevant to Business Visa

Immigration Act

1992

Establishes visa categories; mandates valid passport and visa for all foreign nationals entering Nepal (Section 3).

Immigration Rules

1994

Defines visa subcategories including Business Visa; specifies application and renewal procedures.

Foreign Investment and Technology Transfer Act (FITTA)

2019

Governs foreign direct investment approval; defines eligible sectors and investment thresholds.

Together, these three instruments establish the eligibility criteria, document requirements, fee structures, and compliance obligations that every Business Visa applicant must satisfy. Amendments to FITTA in 2019 significantly liberalised Nepal’s investment framework, making it easier for foreign nationals to obtain investment approval, a prerequisite for the Business Visa.

Who Is Eligible for a Business Visa in Nepal?

Not all foreign nationals who visit Nepal for business purposes qualify for a Business Visa. The Immigration Rules specify that the following categories of foreign nationals are eligible:

  • Foreign nationals who have obtained approval to invest in any trade or industry in Nepal under FITTA 2019.
  • Authorized representatives of foreign companies that have received investment approval from the Department of Industry.
  • Foreign nationals who have obtained permission to carry out export trade from Nepal.
  • Foreign nationals who travel to Nepal from a third country to purchase and export goods manufactured in Nepal, or to place purchase orders for Nepali exports.

⚠️ Important Exception: Indian nationals do not require a Business Visa to enter, reside, or invest in Nepal. This exemption exists under the bilateral treaty between India and Nepal. However, Indian nationals who wish to invest formally must still register their business and comply with Nepalese investment and company laws.

Foreign investors, company directors, shareholders, business consultants, and representatives of foreign companies from countries including the United States, United Kingdom, China, Australia, European Union member states, Japan, South Korea, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, the Philippines, and Myanmar are all eligible to apply, subject to meeting the legal requirements described in this guide.

Step-by-Step Procedure for Obtaining a Business Visa in Nepal

The Business Visa application process in Nepal is a sequential, multi-stage procedure that spans several government departments. Each step must be completed in the correct order, as the output of one step (such as a recommendation letter) becomes a mandatory input for the next. The entire process typically takes between two and six weeks from commencement to visa issuance.

Step 1: Obtain Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) Approval

The first and most foundational step is securing formal approval from the Department of Industry (DOI) to invest in Nepal under the Foreign Investment and Technology Transfer Act (FITTA), 2019. Without this approval, no subsequent steps can proceed.

The FDI approval process involves submitting a formal investment proposal that details:

  • The nature of the proposed business or industry
  • The amount of foreign investment (in NPR and the investor’s home currency)
  • The proposed shareholding structure
  • The intended business sector and specific activities

The Department of Industry will evaluate whether the proposed investment falls within Nepal’s permitted sectors for foreign investment. Certain sectors such as defence, arms manufacturing, and retail trade are restricted or prohibited for foreign investors.

ℹ️ Timeline: FDI approval from the Department of Industry typically takes 7-15 working days, subject to completeness of documentation and the nature of the proposed business.

Step 2: Company Registration, Tax Registration, and Industry Registration

Once FDI approval is obtained, the investor must complete the following three registrations before proceeding to the visa recommendation stage:

  1. Company Registration: Register the business entity with the Office of the Company Registrar (OCR) in Kathmandu. This produces a Certificate of Incorporation and a copy of the Memorandum and Articles of Association.
  2. Industry Registration: Register the specific industry or business activity with the Department of Industry, which produces an Industry Registration Certificate.
  3. Tax Registration: Obtain a Permanent Account Number (PAN) from the Inland Revenue Department, and if applicable, register for Value Added Tax (VAT). These registrations are mandatory for business operations in Nepal.

✅ Pro Tip: These three registrations can sometimes be progressed simultaneously if all required documents are prepared in advance. Engaging a legal professional or consultant familiar with Nepali company law can significantly reduce the time required.

Step 3: Obtain a Business Visa Recommendation Letter from the Department of Industry

This is one of the most critical steps in the entire process. The Department of Industry (or another relevant government line agency, depending on the sector) must issue a formal Recommendation Letter confirming that the applicant is a legitimate investor operating a registered and compliant business in Nepal.

As part of this step, the Department of Industry will typically conduct a physical inspection of the registered business premises to verify that:

  • The business is operational or in active preparation
  • The registered address corresponds to an actual place of business
  • The investment has been or is being genuinely injected into the company

The recommendation letter will specify the recommended visa duration, which the Department of Immigration will then consider when issuing the visa.

⚠️ Critical Note: The physical inspection by the Department of Industry is mandatory and cannot be waived. Ensure your office premises are properly established before requesting the recommendation letter.

Step 4: Submit the Visa Application to the Department of Immigration

With the recommendation letter in hand, the applicant may now submit a formal Business Visa application to the Department of Immigration, located in Maitighar, Kathmandu. The application must be accompanied by the complete set of required documents (detailed in the next section).

The Department of Immigration will review all submitted documents, cross-reference them with records from the Department of Industry, and verify that all information is accurate and consistent. If the application is complete and satisfactory, the Business Visa will typically be issued within one to two working days of document submission.

✔ Processing: Once all documents are submitted and verified, the Department of Immigration typically issues the Business Visa within 1-2 working days.

Complete List of Required Documents

Submitting a complete, accurate, and consistent set of documents is the single most important factor in ensuring a smooth and successful Business Visa application. Incomplete or inconsistent documentation is the primary cause of delays and rejections. The following documents are required:

Documents Required for a First-Time Application

  1. Recommendation letter from the Department of Industry or relevant government line agency
  2. Bio-data (personal details) of the visa applicant, required for first-time applicants only
  3. Foreign Investment Acceptance Letter issued by the Department of Industry
  4. Certificate of Company/Industry Registration
  5. Memorandum and Articles of Association of the company
  6. Certificate of PAN (Permanent Account Number) registration
  7. Tax clearance certificate from the Inland Revenue Department
  8. Certified copy of company bank account operation certificate
  9. Copy of the applicant’s passport (main biographical data page)
  10. Copy of the applicant’s most recent visa (if previously visited Nepal)
  11. Industry monitoring and supervision report from the Department of Industry or relevant line agency
  12. Proof of foreign investment, bank transaction documents confirming the investment amount has been remitted
  13. Shareholder register as recorded by the Office of the Company Registrar (mandatory for investments above NPR 10 million)

Additional Documents Required for Renewal Applications

  • Audit report with balance sheet for the most recent financial year
  • Progress report of the company/industry
  • Latest tax clearance certificate
  • Updated industry monitoring report
  • Extension approval (where applicable)

ℹ️ Document Consistency: Ensure that the company name, address, and registration numbers are identical across all submitted documents. Any discrepancy, even a minor spelling variation, can trigger delays or additional verification requirements.

Business Visa Fees in Nepal (2025)

The government fees for a Business Visa in Nepal are structured according to the amount of investment made by the applicant. Higher investment levels attract lower visa fees, reflecting Nepal’s policy of incentivising larger foreign investment. All fees are payable in US Dollars (USD).

⚠️ Important: Applicants who have invested more than NPR 10 million (approximately USD 75,000) must submit Share Details (the shareholder register) as a mandatory additional document, in addition to the standard document set.

In addition to the government visa fees, applicants should budget for ancillary costs including professional legal fees if engaging an immigration lawyer or consultant, document translation and notarisation costs, and travel expenses related to the DOI inspection visit.

Processing Time: How Long Does It Take?

The total time from commencing the Business Visa process to receiving the visa depends heavily on how efficiently each stage is completed, whether all documents are prepared in advance, and the current workload of the relevant government departments. The following provides a realistic timeline:
